text: Up to now, you've built flows as a maker inside your own environment. This lesson switches hats: you're the IT admin at Castlebridge Logistics, responsible for governing every flow every dispatcher, warehouse supervisor, and finance clerk across the company builds, not just your own.

Makers and admins use two different tools, and it's important you know which one you're in. Makers build and run their own flows at make dot powerautomate dot com, seeing only their own work. Admins govern everything tenant-wide, every environment, every policy, every flow across the whole company, from a separate tool: the Power Platform Admin Center.

The admin center's navigation pane groups every governance task into feature areas: Manage, Security, Copilot, Monitor, Deployment, Licensing, and Support. Underneath Manage sits one of the most important concepts in this chapter: the environment, a container that isolates a set of flows and data from every other environment. That isolation is the single biggest lever an admin has for limiting the damage a bad flow can cause.

A DLP policy classifies every connector as Business, Non-Business, or Blocked, and stops a single flow from mixing them, so nobody at Castlebridge can wire their SQL Server shipment data straight into a personal Twitter post. The Monitor page shows flow health across the whole tenant, not just one flow, and the Actions page separately surfaces Microsoft's own recommendations for improving your tenant's security and reliability before small problems grow.

A maker only ever sees their own flow's run history; an admin, from the admin center, sees all of it across the entire organization. Next up, lesson twenty-nine: how Castlebridge actually moves a flow safely from a Test environment into Production.
